w1.title: Worked Example 1: Balanced vs Unbalanced Forces & Inertia (First Law)
w1.question: Why does a passenger lean forward when a moving bus brakes suddenly?

steps.text: Before braking, both passenger and bus move forward at the same velocity.
Brakes apply a backward force to the bus floor, slowing the feet immediately.
By inertia of motion, the upper body continues moving forward.

opts.m: Higher mass always means greater inertia.

w2.title: Worked Example 2: Momentum & Newton's Second Law (F = ma)
w2.question: What net force is required to accelerate a 5 kg cart at 3 m/s²?

steps.text: Given mass m = 5 kg and acceleration a = 3 m/s².
Apply Newton's Second Law: F = m × a.

check.q: Why does a cricketer pull their hands back while catching a fast ball?

opts.t: To increase stopping time and reduce impact force

opts.m: The momentum change is fixed by initial velocity.
Shorter stopping time causes a larger painful force.

w3.title: Worked Example 3: Action-Reaction Pairs & Conservation of Momentum
w3.question: Why do action and reaction forces never cancel each other out?

steps.text: Action force is exerted by Body A on Body B.
Reaction force is exerted by Body B on Body A.
Because they act on two different objects, they do not cancel on a single object.

check.q: In an isolated collision between two carts, what remains conserved?

opts.t: Total linear momentum of the system

opts.m: Total momentum m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ is conserved.

NODES.title: Balanced vs Unbalanced Forces & Inertia (First Law)

steps.title: Balanced vs Unbalanced Forces & Inertia (First Law)
steps.body: An object stays at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force. Mass is the measure of inertia.

opts.m: Higher mass always means greater inertia.

steps.title: Momentum & Newton's Second Law (F = ma)
steps.body: Momentum is p = m × v. The rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to net applied force: F = m × a (in Newtons).

steps.title: Action-Reaction Pairs & Conservation of Momentum
steps.body: To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction acting on two different bodies, so total momentum of an isolated system stays constant.
